title: Homotopy invariance of each fixed-type hammock graph
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and weak homotopy equivalences of simplicial sets as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Use the ordinary fixed-word diagram categories and their nerves from [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. A wide simplicial subcategory has the same objects, simplicial subsets of the mapping sets, and contains identities and composites. Let $O$ be a small set, let $A,B$ be simplicial categories with object set $O$, let $U\subseteq A$, $V\subseteq B$ be wide simplicial subcategories, and let $S:A\to B$ fix objects and send $U$ into $V$. Assume that for every $a,b\in O$ both $A(a,b)\to B(a,b)$ and $U(a,b)\to V(a,b)$ are weak homotopy equivalences. Fix $x,y\in O$ and a finite word $w=(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_l)$ with letters $+$ and $-$. Define the bisimplicial set $D^w_{A,U}(x,y)_{p,q}$ to consist of commutative rectangular diagrams in the ordinary category $A_p$ with $q+1$ rows, $l$ horizontal columns, and endpoints $x,y$ in every row. All vertical arrows point down and belong to $U_p$, and the endpoint vertical arrows are identities. Column $i$ points right if $\epsilon_i=+$, and left with its arrows in $U_p$ if $\epsilon_i=-$. Identity columns and adjacent columns of the same direction are allowed; no reduction is imposed. In the $p$ direction apply the simplicial operators of $A,U$; in the $q$ direction delete or repeat rows, composing the intervening vertical arrows when a row is deleted. The length-zero diagram exists exactly when $x=y$. Define $D^w_{B,V}$ in the same way. Applying $S$ to every arrow gives a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\operatorname{diag}D^w_{A,U}(x,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{diag}D^w_{B,V}(x,y)$$
for every $w,x,y$.
